_provenance.description: Impulse SVI vs NumPyro SVI on the three continuous PPLBench models (logistic_regression, robust_regression, n_schools) under the SVI PPLBench protocol. Re-run 2026-07-13 (suffix 'b') after fixing the n_schools guide-draw column-ordering bug documented below. Supersedes svi_pplbench_results_2026-07-13.json.
_provenance.config: pplbench_configs/svi/{logistic_regression,robust_regression,n_schools}.json. Model blocks copied verbatim from pplbench_configs/standard/*.json so data matches the NUTS runs: logistic_regression n=10000 k=10 rho=3.0 seed 12345; robust_regression n=10000 k=10 seed 12345; n_schools n=10000 seed 12345. SVI harness: iterations=200 (K=200 posterior draws from fitted guide), num_warmup=0, trials=4.
_provenance.infer_args: step_size=0.01, num_steps=2000 (SVI optimization budget), num_particles=1, init_scale=0.1, guide=AutoNormal, optimizer=Adam (identical for both arms). Both arms start the guide from the SAME deterministic point: unconstrained loc = 0 (Impulse: initial_position=zeros; NumPyro: init_to_value(constrain(0)) via _svi_init_constrained), init_scale converted to softplus_inv(0.1) on both sides. Init/transform/Jacobian/ELBO were already matched; see root_cause.
_provenance.protocol: PPLBench trials-as-chains: overall n_eff = arviz.ess (min/median/max over all latent params, 4 trials as 4 chains); n_eff/s median = overall n_eff median / steady-state (trials 1..3) inference wall time; PLL = per-trial final cumulative predictive log-likelihood on the held-out test items using the K=200 guide draws. Only the guide FIT is timed.
_provenance.root_cause: The 28x-worse n_schools held-out PLL in the 2026-07-13 run was NOT a guide-initialization difference (both arms already start from unconstrained loc=0, use ExpTransform for positive sites, and include the Jacobian correction; the two arms' ELBO trajectories are near-identical at every checkpoint and converge to the same value). It was a POST-FIT COLUMN-ORDERING bug in the Impulse harness. The C++ VI lowering lays the fitted loc/scale (and per-step trace) out in model DECLARATION order among selected sites (collectSupportInfoForSelection with positionDeclarationOrder=true, ExpandImpulsePass.cpp:2622-2624; required so the guide's per-site RNG draw order matches NumPyro). But the Julia post-fit path (harness.jl svi_guide_draws + ProbProg.filter_entries_by_selection + unflatten_trace) indexed the guide's output columns in the ALPHABETIZED select() order used by the NUTS I/O boundary (Reactant.jl/src/probprog/Types.jl:293 sorts addresses; Utils.jl:209 accumulates offsets in that order). For n_schools the three HalfCauchy scales (sigma_state, sigma_district, sigma_type) are DECLARED FIRST (columns 0,1,2) but SORT LAST alphabetically, so the harness applied the per-site exp() bijector to the wrong (real beta) columns and read each sigma site's value from the wrong column. Result: the reported sigma sites were exp() of small real beta locs (collapsed near 0), and the reported beta_baseline (+1.082) was actually the raw unconstrained sigma_state loc (exp(1.082)=2.95 = the true sigma_state). logistic_regression (alpha,beta) and robust_regression (alpha,beta,nu,sigma) were unaffected because for them declaration order == alphabetical order, so the exp() bijector landed on the correct columns even though nu/sigma are positive-support.
_provenance.fix: harness.jl: added svi_selected_entries(entries, selection), which mirrors ProbProg.filter_entries_by_selection but walks tt.entries in DECLARATION order (matching build_selection_attr's all_addresses order that the C++ VI position layout follows) and accumulates offsets in that order. run_svi now builds selected_entries via svi_selected_entries instead of filter_entries_by_selection, so svi_guide_draws (exp bijector) and unflatten_trace (column->site mapping) agree with the guide's actual declaration-order column layout. The NUTS path (still uses filter_entries_by_selection, alphabetical) is untouched, matching its positionDeclarationOrder=false layout. Pure Julia change in the benchmark harness; no native rebuild.
_provenance.command: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' ./run_pplbench.sh --device cpu --threads 32 svi/<model>  (default arms: numpyro + impulse; optional 'Impulse (no opt)' skipped).
_provenance.env: conda probprog-bench python (numpyro 0.19.0 / jax) for NumPyro; Julia + Reactant.jl @ oopsla/Reactant.jl (post-migration stack, native build as of 2026-07-10; unchanged, only harness.jl edited) for Impulse. CPU only (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''), 32 threads.
